title: Jubilant Charred Venezuelan Cashew Tagine
description: A festive and diabetic-friendly Venezuelan dish featuring charred cashew nuts, this tagine is a perfect blend of flavors and textures, with a unique ice-bath-shock step to achieve the signature bouncy qq texture.
instructions: Heat the olive oil in the clay tagine over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion and cook until it is translucent and starting to caramelize.
Add the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly to prevent burning.
Stir in the ground cumin, coriander, smoked paprika, salt, and black pepper, and cook for 1 minute.
Add the raw cashew nuts and cook, stirring frequently, until they are charred and fragrant, about 5 minutes.
Add the low-sodium chicken broth to the tagine and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer, covered, for 20 minutes, or until the cashews have achieved the desired bouncy qq texture.
Remove the tagine from the heat and immediately submerge it in an ice bath to stop the cooking process and achieve the signature charred texture.
Let the tagine cool to room temperature, then refrigerate it for at least 2 hours to allow the flavors to meld.
Serve the Jubilant Charred Venezuelan Cashew Tagine chilled, garnished with fresh herbs if desired.
